intro: Automate bulk code tasks by scripting Codex across files, packages, and repos.

sections.title: Process Multiple Files
sections.code:
#!/bin/bash
# Add missing return types to TypeScript files, one by one

FILES=$(find src -name "*.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*" -not -name "*.d.ts")

for FILE in $FILES; do
  echo "Processing $FILE..."
  codex --approval-mode full-auto --quiet \
    "Add explicit TypeScript return types to all functions in $FILE \
     that are missing them. Do not change any logic."

  # Revert if type-check fails
  npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -q "error" && \
    echo "Type error in $FILE — reverting" && git checkout "$FILE"
done

echo "Done. Review: git diff"

sections.title: Apply the Same Change Across Repos
sections.code:
#!/bin/bash
REPOS=("~/projects/api" "~/projects/worker" "~/projects/frontend")
TASK="Add error handling to all fetch() calls — wrap in try/catch"

for REPO in "${REPOS[@]}"; do
  cd "$REPO" || continue
  git checkout -b "codex/error-handling-$(date +%Y%m%d)"
  codex --approval-mode full-auto --quiet "$TASK"
  npm test && git commit -am "feat: add error handling" || echo "Tests failed in $REPO"
  cd - > /dev/null
done

sections.title: Generate Tests for Untested Files
sections.code:
#!/bin/bash
# Find files with no corresponding test
for FILE in $(find src/lib -name "*.ts" -not -name "*.test.ts"); do
  TEST="${FILE%.ts}.test.ts"
  [ -f "$TEST" ] && continue

  echo "Generating tests for $FILE..."
  codex --approval-mode full-auto \
    "Write a Jest test file for $FILE. Save it to $TEST.
     Cover: happy path, error cases, edge cases."
done

items.title: Always branch first
items.body: git checkout -b codex/task-name before any automated Codex run. git checkout . to reset if things go wrong.

items.title: Gate every step with tests
items.body: codex '...' && npm test || (git checkout . && exit 1) — never let broken code accumulate.

items.title: Keep tasks hardcoded, not from input
items.body: Never pipe untrusted user input into TASK=... Task strings should be literals or sanitised variables.
